samples.summary: The stated outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started") is not met for any value ≥ 1000, and the residue that remains permanently changes what the cell displays — the same one-way `nf` defect the issue reports.
samples.evidence: `unsetKeepsRendering` compares the post-step rendering against the unset rendering, not against the cell's ORIGINAL rendering. For `1234.5` with no style: Increase writes `{dp: 2, nf: 'number'}` → the cell now displays `1,234.50` (formatValue's `number` case uses `toLocaleString`, which groups: format.ts:221). Decrease then refuses the unset precisely BECAUSE dropping `nf` would flatten `1,234.5` → `1234.5` — i.e. it refuses in order to preserve a grouping the buttons themselves introduced and that the user never asked for. The cell ends at `{dp: 1, nf: 'number'}` displaying `1,234.5` where it started at `1234.5`, and no sequence of the two buttons can get it back. `packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts` ('should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten') pins this as intended, and docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:222-232 declares it an accepted deviation. The rationale is circular for the un-styled starting state: the thing being protected is an artefact of the Increase, so 'rendering wins' does not actually protect the user's original rendering here. Since grouped values are ordinary spreadsheet data, this leaves the reported bug class unfixed for a large share of real cells.

samples.summary: Unrelated bug fix bundled in: `compactCell` now carries the four spill fields, plus a new spill test file. Nothing in the decimal round-trip issue or its todo asks for this, and no design doc records the new invariant.
samples.evidence: The diff adds spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked preservation to `compactCell` and a `Sheet spill metadata` suite in packages/sheets/test/model/style-mutation.test.ts. The dropped-spill-on-style-write bug pre-dates this change (`setStyle` already went through `compactCell`, sheet.ts:3715), so it is a separate defect riding along with #845. docs/design/sheets/calculator.md:59-66 documents the spill metadata but is not updated with the 'style-only rewrites must preserve spill fields' invariant, and docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md gets only a source-comment-level mention.

samples.summary: Scope creep in `format.ts`: a three-tier `safeFormat` degradation ladder and a hostile-input test suite are added, neither of which the decimal round-trip issue asks for.
samples.evidence: safeFormat gains locale→options→bare-number fallbacks and `formatValue` gains `clampDecimals`; `format.test.ts` gains a 'formatValue hostile input' describe block for rejected locales/currencies. Only the *stepping* clamp is traceable to the issue (a stored `NaN`/`400` would wedge `changeDecimals`); the locale/currency robustness work is an independent hardening task folded into this PR, widening the blast radius of a bug-fix change and making the revert unit larger than the fix.

samples.summary: The `defaultKeys` pinning path makes `setRangeStyle` write per-cell styles across the selection, contradicting the layer model that section of the design doc states.
samples.evidence: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md (unchanged section, ~line 76) promises that a cell selection 'append[s] a `rangeStyles` patch and only touch[es] existing cell-level styles that conflict with the patch (to avoid redundant writes)'. `collectStyleValuesToPin` + the `setStyle` loop now materialise an inherited `nf` onto every populated cell in the selection whose effective value differs, purely because the appended patch sits above the column/row/sheet layers. That is a workaround at the wrong layer: the alternative (not putting the default-only key in the range patch at all, or resolving defaults per patch layer) keeps the inheritance model intact. As written, one decimal click on a wide selection can convert inherited formatting into thousands of explicit cell-level styles.

samples.summary: `setRangeStyle`'s own design-doc section is not updated for its new `options.defaultKeys` parameter and pinning behaviour; the semantics are described only inside the decimals subsection.
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleValues` correctly gets a sibling section under the write-semantics headings, but the signature change to the central `setRangeStyle` API (new second argument, new default-vs-override distinction, new cell-level pinning) appears only in the 'Increase / decrease decimal places' narrative further down. A reader of the `setRangeStyle` section learns nothing about the new mode.

samples.summary: The fix trades cell-level residue for layer-level residue: emptied column/row/sheet styles are persisted as `{}` because `Store` has no delete for those layers, and no Store extension was proposed.
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleValues` writes `omitStyleKeys(...)` results back via `setColumnStyle`/`setRowStyle`/`setSheetStyle`; packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:127-149 exposes no delete for these, so an all-keys-removed layer stays as an empty object forever and `getStyle` starts returning `{}` where it returned `undefined` (resolveEffectiveStyle, sheet.ts:916 short-circuits on truthiness). The design doc acknowledges this and asserts 'every consumer reads keys off it optionally', but the issue is about eliminating residue, and this introduces a new residue state in the persisted (Yorkie-replicated) model rather than extending the store interface.

samples.summary: Removing `dp: 2` from `DefaultStyleValues` changes pruning for every `dp` writer in the repo, not just the decimal buttons.
samples.evidence: `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys` no longer prunes `dp: 2`, so xlsx import (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:229,239,243,250,252) and any toolbar number-format write now persist `dp: 2` where it was previously dropped. The rationale (keeping 'no dp' distinguishable from 'dp: 2' for `explicitDp`) is sound and documented, but the consequence reaches well beyond the decimals feature and is only stated as a code comment plus a doc bullet; consumers such as packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:62 still hardcode `dp === 2` as 'default', so the two notions of default now live in two places.

samples.summary: `getActiveDecimalPlaces` is dead and now duplicates part of `getActiveDecimalState`; the diff updates it instead of removing it.
samples.evidence: grep for `getActiveDecimalPlaces` finds only its own definition/doc-comment in sheet.ts — no caller in sheets, frontend, or tests. The diff adds `clampDecimals` to it, keeping a second, weaker answer to 'what dp does the active cell have' alongside `getActiveDecimalState` (knip does not flag unused class methods, so nothing else will catch it).

samples.summary: Helper placement and half-finished extraction: `omitStyleKeys` lands in range-styles.ts while its siblings (`compactCell`, `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys`) live in style-mutation.ts, `withoutSetDefaults` is a private function inside the already-huge sheet.ts, and the new `selectionTargets()` helper leaves the two pre-existing inline copies of the same expression untouched.
samples.evidence: `selectionTargets()` (sheet.ts:4445-ish) reproduces `this.ranges.length > 0 ? this.ranges : [this.getRangeOrActiveCell()]`, which still appears verbatim in `setRangeStyle` (sheet.ts:3788) and `resetRangeStyleToDefault` (sheet.ts:3861). `withoutSetDefaults` is a pure style transform and belongs with the other pure style helpers rather than in the 4900-line sheet.ts.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checkable particular. `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4414-4442) compares the unset rendering against the post-step rendering, never against the cell's original rendering, and `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4331-4349) only unsets when that comparison passes. `format.ts:218-225` confirms `nf: 'number'` groups via `toLocaleString` while the plain path returns the raw value (format.ts:205-211), so for `1234.5` the unset is refused and the cell is left at `{dp: 1, nf: 'number'}` rendering `1,234.5` where it started at `1234.5`. Hand-tracing both button directions from that residue shows no sequence returns to unstyled (Increase→dp:2, Decrease→refused dp:1; Decrease→dp:0, Increase→refused dp:1). The repo itself pins this as intended (decimals.test.ts:94-112) and admits the issue's "exactly as it started" outcome is "knowingly not met" for grouped values (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:11-18; sheet-style.md:224-233, 286-289). The reviewer's circularity point also holds: on a plain starting cell the grouping being protected was introduced by the Increase itself (sheet.ts:4352-4360), so "rendering wins" does not protect the user's original rendering. Unmet acceptance criterion on ordinary spreadsheet data = major under the design-fit rubric; no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.

finding.summary: The issue's outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started", #845) is deliberately narrowed to "wherever restoring inheritance renders identically". Two documented classes still keep a `{dp, nf: 'number'}` residue: values large enough to be grouped (`1234.5`) and any user-chosen `nf: 'number'`. The narrowing is recorded in docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md ("Increase / decrease decimal places") and docs/tasks/active/20260818-...-todo.md rather than met, so if the issue's acceptance table lists a grouped value or a formatted cell, that criterion is unmet. Surfacing so the verifier can check the issue text (which I could not see); if the issue's acceptance only covers the reported ungrouped/unformatted case, this is fully satisfied and can be dropped.
finding.evidence: changeDecimals only unsets when `unsetKeepsRendering`; test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' asserts the `{dp:1, nf:'number'}` residue for '1234.5'.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim in the finding checks out against the tree. sheet.ts:4331-4335 gates the unset on `unsetKeepsRendering`, which (4414-4442) refuses whenever `formatValue` with the keys removed differs from `formatValue` at the step target — so a grouped value and a user-chosen `nf:'number'` retain a `{dp, nf:'number'}` residue. decimals.test.ts:94-112 and :114-127 assert that residue as intended behavior. The narrowing from the issue's absolute outcome is recorded, not met, in docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:214-233 and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-18,100-102. This is a spec-conformance question and therefore in the design-fit lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply; the code is exactly as described, so `not-present` does not apply; there is no guard that makes it unreachable — the refusal path IS the behavior being flagged. The one thing I could not check is the decisive one: issue #845's acceptance table is not in the repository (the todo has no "Acceptance criteria (from the issue)" section, unlike other task files such as docs/tasks/active/20260812-date-display-format-todo.md:18), so I cannot establish whether it lists a grouped or pre-formatted cell. Uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Headline outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started") is knowingly not met for grouped values and user-chosen `nf: 'number'`
finding.evidence: The task doc's outcome is absolute: "Increase decimal places followed by Decrease decimal places must leave a cell exactly as it started — including leaving no dp/nf behind" (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5). The implementation's `unsetKeepsRendering` gate means any value ≥ 1000 (`1234.5`) keeps a `{dp, nf:'number'}` residue after an equal number of increases/decreases — asserted as intended by the new test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:96-113) and recorded as a 'Known deviation' in the todo (:87-89) and in sheet-style.md:262-266. The deviation is documented and argued for, but it is a partial fulfilment of the stated outcome rather than the outcome; a reviewer/verifier should confirm the deviation was accepted on the issue (#845) and not just self-granted in the task file.

verdict.reason: The described behavior exists exactly as claimed. `Sheet.changeDecimals` only restores inheritance when `unsetKeepsRendering` agrees (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4331-4349, 4414-4442); for a grouped value such as 1234.5 the comparison formatValue('1234.5', undefined, undefined) vs formatValue('1234.5','number',1) differs, so the unset is refused and a {dp, nf:'number'} residue survives an equal number of increases/decreases. The new tests assert this as intended (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:94-112 for the grouped value, :114-127 for a user-chosen nf:'number'). The repo's own docs concede the gap: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:214-233 and :280-289 call these 'accepted deviations from the absolute wording of the issue', and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-18, :91-102 say the outcome was 'narrowed during review' and lists it under 'Known deviations'. The reviewer's one inaccuracy is quoting todo:3-5 as stating the absolute outcome (that line actually states the narrowed one), but that is a paraphrase slip, not a refutation of the substance. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, nothing guards it away, and an unmet issue outcome is major-by-kind in the design-fit lane. I could not read issue #845 to confirm whether the narrowing was accepted upstream or self-granted in the task file, so the uncertainty keeps the finding.
